title: Corrected Cone Tip Resistance (qt)

u2.description: Pore pressure measured at shoulder (u2 position)

a.description: Net area ratio of cone (typically 0.70–0.85, cone-specific)

applicability: Essential correction for piezocone (CPTU) data. In clays, u2 can be large → significant correction. In sands, u2 ≈ 0 → qt ≈ qc. Always use qt for interpretation, never raw qc.

title: Normalized Cone Parameters (Robertson 2009)
equation: Qtn = [(qt - σv0) / Pa] × (Pa / σ'v0)^n;  Fr = [fs / (qt - σv0)] × 100%;  Bq = (u2 - u0) / (qt - σv0)

σv0.description: Total vertical stress at test depth

σ'v0.description: Effective vertical stress at test depth

n.description: Stress exponent (0.5 for clean sands, 1.0 for clays; iterate via Ic)

applicability: Used for Robertson SBTn soil behavior type classification. n varies with soil type — Robertson (2009) provides iterative procedure using Ic to determine n.

title: Soil Behavior Type Index (Ic)
applicability: Ic < 1.31: gravelly sand to dense sand. 1.31–2.05: clean sand to silty sand. 2.05–2.60: silty sand to sandy silt. 2.60–2.95: clayey silt to silty clay. 2.95–3.60: silty clay to clay. > 3.60: organic soils/sensitive clays. Ic = 2.6 is approximate boundary between sand-like and clay-like behavior.

title: Undrained Shear Strength from CPT (Clays)

Nkt.description: Cone bearing factor (10–20; typically 12–15 for most clays)

applicability: Site-specific Nkt calibrated against lab vane or triaxial tests preferred. General: Nkt = 14 ± 4. Also: Su = (qt - σv0) / NΔu × (u2-u0) using excess pore pressure approach (NΔu typically 5–10).

title: Effective Friction Angle from CPT (Sands)
applicability: For clean to silty sands (Ic < 2.6). Multiple correlations exist; Kulhawy & Mayne widely used. Typical range: φ' = 28–45° corresponding to qt/σ'v0 = 20–400.

title: Relative Density from CPT (Sands)

Qc.description: Compressibility factor (0.91 for high compress., 1.0 for moderate, 1.09 for low)

applicability: Approximate — sensitive to sand compressibility, mineralogy, and cementation. Use with caution; Dr is not a fundamental parameter.

title: Constrained Modulus from CPT

αM.description: Modulus factor (varies with Ic and Qt)

applicability: Robertson (2009): αM = 14 for Ic < 2.1 (sands); αM varies 2–14 for 2.1 < Ic < 2.6; αM = Qtn when Qtn < 14 for clays. Alternative: M = 1/mv from consolidation tests for calibration.

title: Coefficient of Consolidation from Dissipation Test

T*.description: Time factor at 50% dissipation (T50* ≈ 0.245 for u2 position, Teh & Houlsby)

applicability: From monotonic dissipation tests. t50 from plot of u2 vs. log(time). ch relates to cv by ch = cv × (kh/kv). Typical t50: seconds (sand) to hours (fat clay).

title: OCR from CPT (Clays)

k.description: Empirical constant (0.2–0.5; typically 0.33 for general use)

applicability: For intact clays. k is site-specific — calibrate against oedometer results. Mayne (2007): OCR = 0.33 × (qt - σv0)/σ'v0 is a reasonable first estimate. Also: OCR from Bq or Δu approaches.

title: Liquefaction Screening — CRR from CPT

CRR7.5.description: Cyclic Resistance Ratio for M=7.5 earthquake

applicability: Robertson & Wride (1998) / Youd et al. (2001) method, updated by Boulanger & Idriss (2014). qc1Ncs accounts for fines content via Ic-based correction. Compare CRR to CSR (from seismic loading) for FS against liquefaction. FS < 1.0 = potentially liquefiable.

title: Small-Strain Shear Modulus from Seismic CPT
applicability: SCPT measures Vs at 1-m intervals during CPT advance. G0 is the fundamental stiffness parameter for dynamic and small-strain problems. G/G0 degradation curves then applied for design strain levels.

title: Hydraulic Conductivity Estimate from CPT
equation: log(k) ≈ 1.0 - Ic when 1.0 < Ic < 3.27;  log(k) ≈ -5.0 when Ic > 3.27  [k in m/s]
applicability: Very approximate screening estimate only. Varies over orders of magnitude. Dissipation tests provide better estimates of ch. Use for preliminary seepage assessment and identifying permeable vs. impermeable layers.
